sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Whole-cell electrophysiology: HA-tagged GlyR α3K channels responded comparably to cesium (and strychnine) as untagged GlyR α3K channels; electrophysiological properties described as unaffected.
sites.rationale: The ledger (L1, confirmed by L2) reports an HA tag inserted at '+2 in signal-peptide-processed mature GlyR α3'. The signal peptide spans residues 1–33 (authoritative landmarks), so mature position +1 = full-sequence residue 34 (A) and mature position +2 = full-sequence residue 35 (R). Python confirms seq[34] = R and seq[35] = S, placing the junction at insert_after_residue = 35 (±1 ambiguity acknowledged; both 34 and 35 are extracellular). The site is 221 residues from TM1 (boundary at 256), well clear of any TM constraint, and the large N-terminal extracellular domain of GlyR is the canonical location for epitope tags in this subunit family. Full-length GlyR α3 expressed in a heterologous system with an HA epitope tag inserted at the position corresponding to +2 in the signal-peptide-processed mature protein (mature residue 2 = full-sequence residue 35). L2 explicitly compares HA-tagged vs. untagged GlyR α3K channels.

sources.claim: GlyR constructs are epitope-tagged (c-myc, GlyR α2; HA, GlyR α3), however, recent work demonstrates that epitope tags inserted at positions corresponding +2 in signal peptide processed mature GlyR proteins do not affect the electrophysiological properties of GlyR, as shown recently even for high molecular weight tags such as different fluorescent proteins ( Lemmens et al., 2022 ).

literature_notes: Two ledger lines (L1, L2) both support the same single site — the HA-tag insertion near the N-terminus of the mature extracellular domain of GlyR α3. L1 establishes the construct and the '+2 mature protein' position; L2 provides the direct functional comparison (tagged vs. untagged). No other insertion sites are named or implied in the ledger. The ±1 residue ambiguity (insert_after_residue 34 vs. 35) does not affect the classification: both positions are extracellular, both are far from TM1, and the prompt instructs that a one-residue uncertainty never justifies withholding the site. Residue 35 (R) was chosen as the primary junction because '+2 in the mature protein' most naturally denotes the second mature residue, after which the tag is appended. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions are named in the ledger.
